question: True or false: Morningstar found its own star ratings predicted funds' future returns more reliably than their fees did?
answer: False. Russel Kinnel at Morningstar found the cheapest fifth of funds beat the dearest fifth in every asset class and period tested; star ratings worked most of the time, not always. Stars can rest on just three years of returns, and three years cannot tell skill from luck. A fee is certain.
move: Prefer the cost you can be sure of over a past that may not repeat.
ask: When I choose an investment, do I look at last year's winners or at what it costs me each year?
trap: Trusting ratings built on past winners over a dull cost figure.

notes: Three years, 36 months each: no skill wins 64% of months, real skill 44%.
Ten years each: 51% against 44%. Still the wrong way round.
30 years, a whole career: 51% and 51%. No investor could tell them apart.
300 years each: 50% against 55%, the edge built in. No fund lives that long.
